'''Garda GAA''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club based in [[Dublin]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], founded in 1922. They are the GAA representative team of the [[Garda Síochána]]. Garda have won the [[Dublin Senior Football Championship]] on six occasions in 1927, 1929, 1933, 1934, 1935 and 1948. Garda won the [[Dublin Intermediate Football Championship]] on one occasion in 1986, bringing them back to senior status.<ref name=dub>{{cite web |url=https://www.dublingaa.ie/history/roll-of-honour |title=Roll of Honour |publisher=Dublin GAA |access-date=2020-03-02 |archive-date=2019-12-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210142805/https://www.dublingaa.ie/history/roll-of-honour |url-status=live }}</ref> Garda have also had success as a hurling side, having also won the [[Dublin Senior Hurling Championship]] on six occasions in 1931, 1929, 1928, 1927, 1926 and 1925.<ref name=dub /> Westmanstown Gaels is the juvenile division of the club and was set up in 2005.<ref name=herald>{{cite web |url=https://www.herald.ie/sport/gaa/rebecca-honoured-as-gaels-first-dub-28000711.html |title=Rebecca honoured as Gaels first Dub |publisher=Herald |access-date=2020-03-02 |archive-date=2020-03-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302202159/https://www.herald.ie/sport/gaa/rebecca-honoured-as-gaels-first-dub-28000711.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==History==
The Garda GAA was founded in 1922 shortly after the [[Garda Síochána|Civic Guard]], later renamed the Garda Síochána, was established to replace the [[Royal Irish Constabulary]], with responsibility for policing the newly established [[Irish Free State]]. The first [[Garda Commissioner]], [[Eoin O'Duffy]], supported the creation of the club as a way to engage with the community, aiding community policing.<ref name=ie>{{cite web |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/book-highlights-role-garda-played-in-gaa-470881.html |title=Book highlights role Garda played in GAA |publisher=Irish Examiner |access-date=2020-03-02 |archive-date=2020-03-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302194030/https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/book-highlights-role-garda-played-in-gaa-470881.html |url-status=live }}</ref> There were originally doubts as to whether officers of the Gardaí could join the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]], due to [[Rule 21]] banning Crown servants or British security services joining, however the GAA interpreted it to allow members of the Garda Síochána and [[Irish Army]] to join.<ref>{{cite book |first=Gearoid |last=Ó Tuathaigh |title=The GAA and Revolution in Ireland |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IQiWDwAAQBAJ&dq=garda+gaa+1922&pg=PT156 |publisher=Gill & Macmillan Ltd |year=2015 |isbn=978-1848895102}}</ref> O'Duffy also encouraged promising young Gaelic games players to join the police side in Dublin so they were eligible to play for [[Dublin GAA]] in county matches.<ref name=ie /> When Dublin won the [[1927 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]] at [[Croke Park]] against [[Cork GAA]], they had fourteen Garda members on their team, a record for the number of county players from the same club.<ref name=ie /> Membership was originally only open to serving members of the Garda but this restriction was later removed.<ref>{{cite web|last=Donnelly |first=Dave |url=https://dublingazette.com/sport/sport-fingal/westmanstown-tribute-to-twomey/ |title=Westmanstown tribute to Twomey |publisher=Dublin Gazette |access-date=2020-03-02}}</ref>

Since 2002, Garda GAA have played an annual match against the [[Police Service of Northern Ireland]]'s [[PSNI GAA]] following the abolition of Rule 21.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/northern-ireland/psni-and-garda-in-croke-park-clash-28685283.html |title=PSNI and Garda in Croke Park clash |publisher=Belfast Telegraph |access-date=2020-03-02 |archive-date=2020-03-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302194945/https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/northern-ireland/psni-and-garda-in-croke-park-clash-28685283.html |url-status=live }}</ref> They play for the McCarthy cup named after [[Thomas St George McCarthy]], a Royal Irish Constabulary policeman who helped to found the GAA.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/gaa/psni-lined-up-for-historic-croker-date-with-garda-28681735.html |title=PSNI line up for historic Croker date with Garda |publisher=Belfast Telegraph |access-date=2020-03-02 |archive-date=2020-03-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302203518/https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/gaa/psni-lined-up-for-historic-croker-date-with-garda-28681735.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2005, they united with Westmanstown Gaels youth team to provide youth Gaelic games at Garda for the first time.<ref name=herald />

'''Faughs GAA Club''' ({{langx|ga|CLG Fág an Bealach}}) is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] (GAA) [[hurling]] and [[camogie]] club in [[Templeogue]], [[Dublin]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Faughs - Club Information - Dublin GAA |url=https://www.dublingaa.ie/clubs/faughs |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=www.dublingaa.ie}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=WATCH: The people of Faughs GAA on what the club means to them |url=https://www.sportsjoe.ie/gaa/the-people-of-faughs-gaa-club-205038 |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=SportsJOE.ie |date=4 September 2019 |language=en}}</ref> They have won 31 titles.

==History==
{{no references|section|date=December 2024}}
Faughs GAA Club was founded in [[Easter]] 1885 in the [[Phoenix Park]] in Dublin. Its inaugural meeting was held at 4 Gardiner's Row, home of [[Michael Cusack (Gaelic Athletic Association)|Michael Cusack]]. The club name, Faughs, is derived from the [[Irish language]] slogan, {{lang|ga|fág an bealach}}, anglicized as [[Faugh A Ballagh]], meaning "clear the way".

When the Dublin County Board was formed in 1886, Larry O'Toole was on the committee. At this time the Faughs colours were amber and black, and the club played both [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football|football]]. The Faughs took part in the first Dublin championships in 1887, and were winners of the [[Dublin Senior Football Championship]] in 1889.

=== Merge with Davitts ===
In January 1891, Faughs merged with the "[[Davitts GAA|Davitts]]" who, like Faughs, were mostly "spirit grocers assistants". As the "Faughs–Davitts" they adopted a tri-colour amber, black and blue kit. They won their first Dublin senior hurling championship in 1892, and were beaten by [[Redmonds GAA|Redmonds]] of Cork in the All-Ireland final in an unfinished match. The Faughs–Davitts coalition declined after this match.

=== Reorganisation, 1895-1920s ===
In 1895, a number of members of the original Faughs club revived and reorganised the club.{{fact|date=December 2024}} After 1895, Faughs became a hurling-only club and adopted the colours of saffron and green, which it has kept to the present day.

In the early 20th century, the club won the first four senior championships (a four-in-a-row lasting from 1900 to 1904) and another five before 1920. Players during this period included Jack and Jimmy Cleary, [[Danny McCormack (hurler)|Danny McCormack]], Andy Harty, and Jack and Will Connolly. [[Harry Boland]], known for his part in the 1916 Rising, War of Independence and Civil War, also played for Faughs on the 1914 and 1915 championship teams.

A four-in-a-row was achieved again in 1920–1923. In 1920, they won three titles: the Senior Championship and League, Intermediate Championship and League. The team was led by [[Bob Mockler]] and captured the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] title beating [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final by six points. The final score was 4–9 to 4–3. Included in this team were Jim "Builder" Walsh, [[Tommy Moore (hurler)|Tommy Moore]], [[Mick Neville (hurler born 1891)|Mick Neville]], [[Martin Hayes (hurler)|Martin Hayes]], Tom Hayes, Jimmy Cleary, Ned Tobin, [[Bob Doherty]] and [[John Joe Callanan]], who would later captain [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] to beat [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] in the 1930 All-Ireland final.{{fact|date=December 2024}}

=== Mid- to late-20th century ===
From 1939 to 1952, Faughs won eight championships, including two threes-in-a-row in 1939–1941 and 1944–1946. These teams included a number of inter-county and inter-provincial players, including [[Ned Wade (hurler)|Ned Wade]], [[Mick Butler (Dublin hurler)|Mick Butler]], [[Terry Leahy]], [[Mick Gill]], [[Dan Canniffe]], [[Dan Devitt]], [[Jim Prior (hurler)|Jim Prior]], [[Tony Herbert]], Jack Sheedy and Tommy Boland.{{fact|date=December 2024}}

Faughs' next senior championship success had to wait until 1970. They then won several championships in a row. They beat St. Vincents in [[Croke Park]] to win the 1970 title. In May 1971, after a gruelling game, they were beaten by one point by Buffers Alley in the [[Leinster Senior Club Hurling Championship]]. A few days later, they were knocked out of the Dublin championship, again by a single point margin by Craobh Ciaran who went on to win their first Dublin title.

Faughs won the next two county championships of 1972 and 1973 and reached the final in 1974, which they lost to Kilmacud Crokes by one point. Two senior titles came in the 1980s—1986 and 1987. Two more came in the 1990s, 1992 and 1999, to bring the total of senior championship titles to 31.{{fact|date=December 2024}}

== Grounds ==
From their foundation in 1885 up to 1949, Faughs trained in the Phoenix Park in the Fifteen Acres, Nine Acres, Polo Ground and beside the Hurling Ground or Army Ground, except for a short period in the winter of 1942–1943 when they moved to Dolphin Park. From 1949 to 1958, they leased a ground in St. Anne's Estate in Killester, where they erected their own dressing rooms.{{fact|date=December 2024}}

'''Ahane GAA Club''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club in Lisnagry, [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club is affiliated to the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick County Board]] and fields teams in both [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]].

==History==

Located in the [[Ahane, County Limerick|Ahane]], [[Castleconnell]] and [[Montpelier, County Limerick|Montpelier]] areas of [[County Limerick|East Limerick]], Ahane GAA Club was founded on 22 November 1926.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ahanegaa.ie/history|title=Club history|publisher=Ahane GAA website|date=|accessdate=13 June 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> The new club played its first ever match three weeks later, but lost out to [[Newport GAA|Newport]]. The Ahane GAA Club committee affiliated both junior and senior teams for the respective championships in 1927.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lovecastleconnell.com/an-caislean/2011/ahane-gaa-club-a-brief-history/|title=Ahane GAA Club – A brief History|publisher=Love Castleconnell website|date=|accessdate=13 June 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

The Ahane club was in its infancy when it made the breakthrough by winning the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] title after a defeat of [[Croom GAA|Croom]] in 1931. This victory ushered in an unprecedented 25-year period of success. Ahane won seven successive Limerick SHC titles between 1933 and 1939.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/features/196608/Ahane-GAA-honours-great-Limerick-hurling.html|title=Ahane GAA honours great Limerick hurling supporter Gerry, 90|publisher=Limerick Live|date=5 April 2014|accessdate=13 June 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> Defeat by Croom in successive finals was followed by Ahane claiming another seven successive titles between 1942 and 1948.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/portumna-rise-above-the-rest/26522934.html|title=Portumna rise above the rest|publisher=Irish Independent|date=22 March 2009|accessdate=13 June 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> The club also won five successive [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|Limerick SFC]] titles between 1935 and 1939.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.clubinfo.ie/club/ahane-hc/|title=Ahane HC|publisher=Club Info|date=|accessdate=13 June 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

Ahane won their 16th Limerick SHC title in 1955, a victory which put them at the top of the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Roll of honour|all-time roll of honour]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Limerick/ClubTitles|title=Club Titles - Limerick|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=|accessdate=13 June 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> After dominating the championship since their foundation, Ahane failed to win another title until 1998.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/memories-of-mackey-as-ahane-end-famine-26174934.html|title=Memories of Mackey as Ahane end famine|publisher=Irish Independent|date=21 September 1998|access-date=15 October 2018}}</ref> The club retained the title in 1999, before winning a record-setting 19th Limerick SHC in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/tempers-flare-as-ahane-win-26134015.html|title=Tempers flare as Ahane win|publisher=Irish Independent|date=4 October 1999|access-date=15 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10045652.html|title=Ahane kingpins win 19th title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=11 October 2004|access-date=15 October 2024}}</ref>

'''Adare GAA''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] (GAA) club based in [[Adare]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club fields teams in both [[Hurling|hurling]] and [[Gaelic football|football]] and has a strong record in county and provincial competitions.

Adare have reached the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|County Senior Hurling Final]] on 12 occasions. After losing the finals of 1968, 1986, 1990, 1993 and 1996, they finally won their first championship in 2001 and successfully defended it in 2002. In 2003, they narrowly missed out on winning three county titles in a row after losing out to [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] in the final. However, Adare managed to complete a historic 3-in-a-row in 2007 and 2008 and 2009. 
2008 marked their first win in the [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship]] when they overcame [[Toomevara GAA|Toomevara]]. They were subsequently defeated in the Munster Final by [[De La Salle GAA|De La Salle]] on a scoreline of 0–10 to 1-09.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/de-la-salle-complete-epic-comeback-1.917381|title = De la Salle complete epic comeback| newspaper=[[The Irish Times]] }}</ref>

Adare saw a sharp rise in Limerick football prominence winning consecutive promotion through the Junior B, Junior A and Intermediate ranks from 1999, 2000, 2001 respectively. Adare were defeated by Monaleen after a replay in the 2002 [[Limerick Senior Football Championship]]. Adare's second Senior Final appearance was in 2010, where they were again defeated by Monaleen. In 2016, Adare won the Limerick Intermediate Football Championship and subsequently gained promotion back to [[Limerick Senior Football Championship]]. In the same year, Adare then became the first Limerick club to beat Cork opposition in the [[Munster Intermediate Club Football Championship]] overcoming Kiskeam in the Munster Semi-Final.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20430436.html|title = Adare serve notice with skilful show in Mallow|date = 14 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/corkman/sport/gaa/kiskeam-fall-short-to-an-impressive-adare-35221629.html|title = Kiskeam fall short to an impressive Adare}}</ref> Adare were defeated by a formidable [[Kenmare GAA|Kenmare Shamrocks]] team in the Munster Club Final.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20432632.html|title = Kenmare's forward power leaves Adare on the ropes|date = 28 November 2016}}</ref> In 2017, the club won the County Senior Championship for the first time, beating Newcastle West in the Final.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20461436.html|title = Jack English to the rescue in Adare's shock win|date = 23 October 2017}}</ref> In 2018, the club went on to retain the title, becoming the first team in history to win 2 Senior titles immediately following success at Intermediate level. In 2020, Adare then secured a third Senior Championship title beating Ballylanders in the final.{{fact|date=July 2024}}

==Notable players==

[[Declan Hannon]] and [[Ronan Connolly]] are current members of the Limerick senior hurling team and in 2020 were part of the Limerick team that won the Liam MacCarthy. Declan Hannon is the current Limerick Senior Hurling Captain and has led them to All-Ireland glory in 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022. [[Mark Foley (Limerick hurler)|Mark Foley]] has played in 2 all Ireland finals and won 2 all-stars in 1996 and 2001. In 1996 Foley won young player of the year.  He was captain of the Limerick senior team in 2002, 2003, 2008 and 2009. In 2009, he became Limerick's most "capped" ever player when he reached a record 47 senior championship appearances for the county. Other players to have represented Limerick at Senior level include: Timmy Houlihan, Conor Fitzgerald, Jack Foley, Donncha Sheehan, Michael Clifford and Wayne McNamara.

Hugh Bourke, Robbie Bourke, Paul Maher and David Connolly are current{{when?|date=July 2024}} members of the Limerick Senior Football panel.
Other players to have represented Limerick at Senior level include: [[Stephen Lavin]], Aidan O'Rahilly, Neil Mulvihill, Mikey Lyons and Conor Fitzgerald.{{fact|date=July 2024}}

'''Doon GAA club''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club, founded in 1888. It is based in the village of [[Doon, County Limerick|Doon]] in [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club is part of the East Division of the [[Limerick GAA]] and has a tremendous record at underage level and in 2024 has won its first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|County Senior Hurling Championship]]. The club only plays hurling, but footballers in the parish play with neighbouring [[Oola GAA|Oola]]

==Location==
The club is located in the parish of [[Doon, County Limerick|Doon]], mostly in [[County Limerick]] but also containing a few townlands in [[County Tipperary]]; these can play with the other club in the parish, [[Glengar GAA|Glengar]], which is affiliated to the Tipperary GAA County Board. As Oola is only a football club, hurlers from the parish play with Doon. The club is roughly 30 km east of Limerick City. Bordering clubs include [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]], Pallasgreen and Doon's sister club [[Oola GAA|Oola]] in Limerick, and [[Sean Treacy's GAA|Seán Treacy's]], [[Cappawhite GAA|Cappawhite]] and [[Solohead GAA|Solohead]] in Tipperary.

==History==
The club was founded in 1888; it is one of the oldest clubs in the county. The club took part in competitions in both east Limerick and west Tipperary during the late 19th century.

The club's senior hurling team defeated [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] on Sunday 18 November 2007 in Caherconlish, to  become East Limerick Senior Hurling Champions, 2007. They again received the Sean Cunningham Cup. Doon have twice reached the final of the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]], losing to Ballybrown in 1989 and [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] (by only one point) in 2000. In 1973 a Doon player, Willy Moore, was present in the Limerick team which beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Hurling Final|all-Ireland hurling final]].

Doon GAA's under-21 team reached the final of the Limerick Under-21 Hurling Championship in 2004 and lost, but returned to the final in 2005 and beat [[Adare GAA|Adare]] to take the championship for the first time. Doon's success at an underage level is outstanding, winning every county "A" title at each grade. 

On 27 October 2024, Doon made history by beating [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsiagh]] by 0-16 to 2-09 to secure their [[2024 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|first ever]] Limerick Senior Hurling Title.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/1027/1477719-historic-success-for-doon-in-limerick-hurling-final/|title= Historic success for Doon in Limerick hurling final|date=27 October 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=30 October 2024}}</ref>

==Grounds==
The GAA pitch is located just off the main street on the Toher road. The grounds were opened in 1994 and dressing rooms were completed in 2002. The facilities include a full-sized pitch with nets behind each goal, an underage sized pitch with nets behind each goal, a covered stand, four dressing rooms and a hurling wall.

'''De La Salle''' [[Gaelic football]] and [[hurling]] club is based in [[Waterford City]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club competes in [[Gaelic games]] competitions organised by [[Waterford GAA]] board.  The club has won the [[Waterford Senior Hurling Championship]] twice and the [[Waterford Senior Football Championship]] on 6 occasions. While having a notable record in [[gaelic football]], today the club mainly focuses on [[hurling]] and [[camogie]].

==History==

The club takes its name from St. Stephens De La Salle National School in Patrick Street and previous to the current club being established, fielded a hurling team under the name of St. Stephens. St. Stephens won 2 Senior County Hurling Championships, 1913 and 1914.
In recent years the club has concentrated on developing juvenile players and now has one of the biggest under age setups in the South East of Ireland. The club has produced many Senior Inter County hurlers in the last few years such as John Mullane, Johnny and Stephen Brenner, Kevin Moran, Bryan Phelan and Derek McGrath. The club has also won numerous under age County titles in Hurling and Football as well as All Ireland Feile (Under 14 Championships) in both codes.
There were 5 De La Salle players on the Waterford U-21 team which won the counties only U-21 All-Ireland in 1992.

John Barron (1959) is the only De La Salle player to win a Senior All-Ireland hurling medal.

Stephen Brenner, [[John Mullane]], Bryan Phelan and Kevin Moran have won [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] medals with Waterford and also a [[National Hurling League]] Title.

The late Sonny Walsh also won a National League medal with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]]. De La Salle is a family club with famous families like the Brenners, the Daltons and the Duggans part of its core for many years. The club is also very proud of its association with the De La Salle Brothers and wears the crest of St. John Baptist de la Salle on their jerseys.

2008 was an historic year for the club, moving to their new grounds in Gracedieu and winning their first Senior County Hurling title. The club also won the County Under 21 hurling championship and the [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship]]. In December De La Salle were honoured as club of the year in both Waterford and in Munster.
On 21 February 2009 the club made history by being the first club to reach the [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship]] Final at their first attempt when they beat Ruari Og of Cushendall by 1-21 to 1-19 (after extra time) in the All Ireland semi final at [[Parnell Park]] in [[Dublin]]. In November 2010, they won their second [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship]] after a 0-9 to 0-8 win against [[Thurles Sarsfields GAA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/flynn-hails-character-as-de-la-salle-prosper-2440073.html|title=Flynn hails 'character' as De La Salle prosper|date=2010-11-29|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2010-11-30}}</ref>

In 2022, they won the Waterford Senior Camogie Championship for the first time.<ref name="De_La_Salle_v_Gailltír_-_Waterford_Senior_Camogie_Final_2022-1">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2qe1nW7w91g |title=De La Salle v Gailltír - Waterford Senior Camogie Final 2022 |language=en |access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref> In 2023, they could defend the title<ref name="De_La_Salle_v_Gailltír_-_Waterford_Senior_Camogie_Final_2023-1">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ugx8E0qguRc |title=De La Salle v Gailltír - Waterford Senior Camogie Final 2023 |language=en |access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref> and their player [[Beth Carton]] was awarded [[Camogie All Stars Awards#Player of the Year|Camogie Player of the Year]].<ref name="Browne2023-1">{{Cite web |last=Browne |first=P. '''Granagh-Ballingarry GAA''' ({{langx|ga|Greanach-Baile an Gharraí}}) is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club based in west [[County Limerick]], Ireland, within the jurisdiction of [[Limerick GAA]]. The club is situated near Knockfierna Hill, close to the villages of [[Granagh]] and [[Ballingarry, County Limerick|Ballingarry]]. Granagh-Ballingarry GAA was formed in 1990 after the merger between Granagh and Ballingarry GAA clubs. Previously, the clubs had been playing together in some competitions.<ref name="Hoganstand"/>

==Hurling==
[[Hurling]] is the more popular game in the parish. Granagh-Ballingarry are currently (2021) in the Intermediate grade. This is the third tier of the Limerick Hurling Championship. They had enjoyed a period at Senior, after defeating [[Glenroe GAA]] 4–10 to 3–10 in the 2005 Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship.<ref name="Hoganstand">{{cite web |url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=56801 |title=Granagh/Ballingarry braced for senior action |accessdate=16 March 2008 |date=16 February 2006 |publisher=Lynn Publications}}</ref> Granagh-Ballingarry reached the 2006 [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Hurling]] quarter finals, and also in 2007, where they were defeated by Kilmallock. The club were defeated by Garryspillane at the quarter-final stage in 2008 and were defeated by Croom in a round 3 game in 2009. 2010 placed them up against Kilmallock again and the team lost out badly at the quarter-final stage again. The club won their first senior championship in 1911 under the guise of Ballingarry,<ref name="Hoganstand"/> after having won the intermediate championship the year before.<ref name="Hoganstand"/> The club were also finalists in 1896, 1904 and 1912 as Ballingarry, and in 1945 under the current name, Granagh-Ballingarry. In the 1990s the club won several Limerick GAA West Division championships, before winning the Limerick Junior Hurling Championship in 1998.<ref name="Hoganstand"/> The club also won a West Senior Hurling Championship in 2008 defeating Adare.

===Underage hurling===
The minor hurling team has reached two Limerick Minor Hurling Championship finals, firstly in 1971, defeating [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]], before finishing runners-up to Kilmallock in 2006.

'''Caherline GAA''' (Irish: ''Cathair Laighin'') is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club based in [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. It is based in the parish of Caherline/[[Caherconlish]] in the east division of [[Limerick GAA]].

==History==
The club was founded in 1884, making it one of the oldest clubs in county Limerick.<ref>{{cite book |author1=Treacy M. (Ed.) |title=Caherline GAA Club - 100 Years On |date=1984}}</ref> The early years of the club were its most successful, winning the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] on three occasions; 1896, 1905 and 1907. Caherline also lost four county finals in this period; 1889, 1898 (when a lack of crowd control caused the match to be abandoned), 1908 and 1916.

By the 1920s, Caherline had slipped back to the junior ranks but returned to the higher grades in 1927 when winning their first [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship]] by beating [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] in the county final.<ref>{{cite news |title=Limerick Leader |date=31 October 1970 |pages=23}}</ref> This was followed by a second junior title in 1931, when once again Kilmallock were beaten in the final.<ref>{{cite news |title=Limerick Leader |date=23 April 1932 |pages=2}}</ref>

The club went through lean times after this and were not to appear in another county final until 1974 when [[Glenroe GAA|Glenroe]] were the victors in the county junior hurling final.<ref>{{cite news |title=Limerick Leader |date=25 November 1974 |pages=4}}</ref> Caherline were defeated again in the 2001 county junior hurling final, losing out to [[Newcastle West GAA|Newcastle West]]. In 2007, however, Caherline bridged a 76-year gap and claimed their third junior hurling championship title defeating [[Effin GAA|Effin]] on a 3-12 to 1-9 score line in the county final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Reeling in the Years: Limerick GAA’s 2007 |url=https://sportinglimerick.com/reeling-in-the-years-limerick-gaas-2007/ |website=sportinglimerick.com |access-date=16 April 2025 |date=12 June 2020}}</ref>

In 2008, the club played in the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship]] for the first time and reached the county final. However, [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] were to be the victors on this occasion, winning on a score line of 3-14 to 0-15 in Ballyagran on 12 October 2008.<ref>{{cite web |title=Reeling in the Years: Limerick GAA’s 2008 |url=https://sportinglimerick.com/reeling-in-the-years-limerick-gaas-2008/ |website=sportinglimerick.com |access-date=16 April 2025 |date=17 June 2020}}</ref>

By 2016 Caherline were back in the junior ranks but in that year they had a long season in the Limerick junior hurling championship. In the Limerick East division, the club were crowned east junior hurling champions for the first time since 2007 with a 0-14 to 0-11 win over Ballybricken-Bohermore. After defeating Castletown-Ballyagran in the county quarter finals, the club eventually lost out after several replayed games against [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St. Patrick's]] in the semi-finals. This series of games (the original semi-final and two replays) involved last gasp equalisers, extra time, abandonments, red cards over-turned and hard-fought comebacks.Eventually, Caherline lost out after extra time in the second replay on a 1-23 to 3-14 score line on 22 October 2016.<ref>{{cite news |title=Limerick Leader |date=24 October 2016 |pages=26}}</ref>

Caherline won their fourth Limerick junior hurling title in 2021. They progressed from their group of six teams (divisional championships no longer formed part of the county championship after a restructure in 2020) to reach the county quarter finals. In their quarter final, Caherline had a victory over [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] and this was followed by a semi-final win over St. Patrick's. [[St Kieran's GAA (Limerick)|St. Kieran's]] were the opposition in the final, with Caherline winning on a score line of 1-13 to 0-10 in Kilmallock on 13 November 2021.<ref name="LimerickJAHC2021">{{cite web|url = https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/692976/caherline-crowned-limerick-junior-hurling-champions-with-final-win-over-st-kierans.html | website = limerickleader.ie | title = Caherline crowned Limerick junior hurling champions with final win over St Kierans | date = 14 November 2021 | accessdate = 30 July 2024 }}</ref>

'''Feohanagh-Castlemahon''' ({{langx|ga|An Fheothanach – Caisleán Uí Mhathúna}}) is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club located in the parish of [[Mahoonagh]], [[County Limerick]], Ireland. It was founded in 1890.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://feohanaghcastlemahongaa.ie/ | website = feohanaghcastlemahongaa.ie | title = Feohanagh Castlemahon GAA | quote = Feohanagh-Castlemahon is a GAA club located in the parish of Mahoonagh, County Limerick, Ireland. It was founded in 1890 | accessdate = 30 July 2024 }}</ref>  Coolyroe is the main centre for the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]] field, known as Quaid Park.

Hurling is the main sport in Feohanagh-Castlemahon (Fheothanach – Caisleán Uí Mhathúna).  For hurling, [[Mahoonagh]] parish is represented by [[Feohanagh]] and Gaelic football is represented by [[Castlemahon]]. 

There are also handball courts in Coolyroe.

Feohanagh/Castlemahon won the 2011 West Junior A Hurling Championship defeating Dromcollogher/Broadford in the final in Feenagh on 15 October 2011 on a scoreline of 2–10 to 0–08. In 2013, they retained their West Junior A hurling title with a win over neighbours Feenagh/Kilmeedy. However, when the two sides met again in the county final, Feenagh won by 0–14 to 0–11. In 2014 Feohanagh/Castlemahon won the County Junior Championship hurling final beating Na Piarsaigh in a replay on a scoreline of 0-20 to 0-09.

In football in 2013 they were beaten by Glin 0-08 to 0–07 in the West final, but like the hurling that year, the West runners-up won the county final as Castlemahon won on a score line of 1–08 to 1–07, securing intermediate status for 2014. They went on to defeat Drom-Inch of Tipperary and Coolmeen of Clare but were beaten in the Munster Junior Football Championship Final by Keel of Kerry by 0–14 to 0–04.

'''Hospital-Herbertstown''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] (GAA) club in [[County Limerick]], Ireland. The club, which fields both hurling and Gaelic football teams, is based in the South Division close to the border with County Tipperary.{{fact|date=September 2025}} As of 2027, Hospital-Herbertstown will compete in the Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship and the Limerick Junior A Football Championship.

==History==
Founded in 1885, Hospital-Herbertstown is the only club in the history of Limerick GAA to have won the Junior A Football & Hurling double. This was achieved in 1983 with promotion to the Senior ranks in both beating Ardagh in the hurling final and Glin in the football final playing 18 weekends in a row. 

The club reached four County Senior Football finals in the 1990s. The club has also played Senior Hurling on numerous occasions. The clubs greatest achievements, outside of the Junior double, was winning the County Intermediate Hurling Championships in 2000 beating South Liberties in the final and in 2010 beating Dromin/Athlacca in the final to get promoted to Senior.{{fact|date=September 2025}}

Hospital-Herbertstown players to have represented [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] include 2007 All Ireland Final Captain [[Damien Reale]] as well as [[Jimmy Carroll]], Donie Carroll, Liam Garvey, Andy Garvey, PJ Garvey, Aaron Murphy and Paudie Reale.{{fact|date=September 2025}}

'''Kildimo-Pallaskenry GAA''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club located in the villages of [[Kildimo]] & [[Pallaskenry]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]].  It was founded in 1906 and the following are some significant dates from its history:

==History and achievements==
*1906 Pallaskenry affiliated to County Board.
*1912 County Junior hurling final against Claughaun, played in 1914 in Markets Field, Pallaskenry lost 3-2 to 2-3
*1916 Joined with Kildimo.
*1920 Parted from Kildimo.
*1936 West Junior A hurling final against Knockaderry. Pallaskenry lost 7-5 to 1-3.
*1950 Joined Kildimo.
*1951 Pallaskenry field opened and blessed.
*1953 Kildimo/Pallaskenry enter City Division.
*1953 Kildimo/Pallaskenry lost City Junior hurling final to the [[St. Loman's Mullingar GAA|Mental Hospital]] (the Mental Hospital's staff by the way)
*1955 Kildimo/Pallaskenry won City Junior football final, beat Claughaun 0-3 to 0-2.
*1956 Kildimo/Pallaskenry won City Junior hurling final, beat St Patricks 2-7 to 2-4.
*1958 Kildimo/Pallaskenry won City Junior hurling final, beat Ballybrown in replay.
*1959 After Incident in match against Ballybrown, Kildimo/Pallaskenry suspended for five years.
*1965 Kildimo/Pallaskenry back in action, but to no avail.
*1971 Parted from Kildimo- Pallaskenry back on own in West, Kildimo in City Division.
*1980 Pallaskenry field officially purchased.
*1986 Pallaskenry Bord na nÓg formed.
*1987 First underage title, City U13 football win over Ballybrown.
*1989 First underage hurling title, City U12 hurling win over Corpus Christi.
*1992 First County final at any age in 80 years, lost U14 football to Bruree.
*1992 Lost U16 County hurling final to Ballybricken.
*1994 First County championship win ever, Minor football win over Banogue.
*1995 City Junior B football final, lost to Kildimo after replay.
*1996 Won City U21 B football championship beat St. Patricks Ð lost county semi final to Knockainey.
*1997 First competitive adult trophy, won City Junior B Hurling League against Monaleen.
*1997 Won City hurling League Cup Final against Na Piarsaigh.
*1997 Lost County Junior B Hurling semi final to Cappamore.
*1998 Second ever County title, U16 football win over Banogue.
*2001 First championship title Ð City Junior B Football win over St. Patricks.
*2001 Lost County Junior B football quarter final to Castlemahon.
*2002 Lost City Junior B Hurling Championship Final to Monaleen.
*2002 Lost County Junior B Hurling Championship quarter final to Camogue Rovers.
*2006 Won City Junior B Hurling Championship against Mungret.
*2006 Merged with Kildimo, won Minor County Football Championship, Division 1.
*2008 U21 Hurlers beaten by Blackrock in County Final
*2006 Won City Junior B Hurling C'Ship defeating Mungret by 2-7 to 0-9.
*2007 Won City Junior B Hurling C'Ship once more defeating Mungret by 1-8 to 0-10.
*2008 Won City Junior B Hurling C'Ship defeating Claughaun by 0-9 to 1-5.
*2015 After a very successful playing merger with Kildimo, consisting of 10 years at underage level and 4 years at adult level, playing as Kildimo-Pallaskenry, overwhelming majorities at EGMs in both clubs vote in favour of formally disbanding the clubs and to form a brand new club named Kildimo-Pallaskenry.
*2017 Kildimo-Pallaskenry win the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship]] beating Glenroe in the final in Fitzgerald Park, Kilmallock
*2018 The club makes its debut season in the [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship]], ending the season as beaten semi finalists and finishing 2nd in the 8 team group stage.
*2019 Kildimo-Pallaskenry qualify for the Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship Final at the second attempt, topping the group and subsequently beating [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] in the semi-final (after extra time). However, they lost to [[Blackrock GAA|Blackrock]] in the final.
*2020 In a Covid-19 disrupted Premier Intermediate Championship, Kildimo-Pallaskenry secure promotion to the Senior Hurling Championship after defeating [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret St Paul's]] in the final. 
*2021 & 2022 Kildimo Pallaskenry played in a shortened 2021 Championship, again due to COVID-19, failing narrowly to get to the semi finals. However, they win the County Cup defeating [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] in the final. Normality returned in 2022, a regular 6 team group format back in action and after an opening defeat to 2021 Premier Intermediate champions [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret St Paul's]], Kildimo-Pallaskenry end up winning Group 2 and promotion to Group 1 for 2023. They subsequently lose to [[Doon GAA|Doon]] in the Quarter Finals.
*2023 Kildimo-Pallaskenry are playing in the top division of Limerick alongside Patrickswell, Na Piarsaigh, Kilmallock, Ahane and Doon.

'''Fermoy GAA''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] based in the town of [[Fermoy]], [[County Cork]], Ireland.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yourlocal.ie/company/379259837489152|title=Fermoy GAA Club Pairc Mhic Ghearailt, Colmcille Street, Fermoy, County Cork|website=www.yourlocal.ie}}</ref> The club fields teams in competitions organized by the [[Cork GAA]] county board and the [[Avondhu GAA]] divisional board. ==History==
Fermoy Gaelic Athletic Association club was founded in 1886 at a meeting in the National League Rooms (now called Fermoy Commercial club in O'Neill Crowley Quay or present home to the Fermoy Bridge club). He was also one of the Munster delegates to the second All-Ireland Congress held in [[Thurles]] in 1887, and was elected one of the first Vice-Presidents of the GAA National Executive Body.{{fact|date=April 2022}}

Clondulane village in the suburbs of Fermoy was the hub of Fermoy teams at that time, due to the large employment available at the Flour Mills which were situated there for many years.{{citation needed|date=February 2017}}

'''Claughaun GAA''' ({{langx|ga|CLG Chlochán}}) is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] (GAA) club based in St Brigid's parish on the southside of [[Limerick]] City, Ireland. The club was founded  in 1902, in the Poulin/Pennywell area of St John's parish. It fields teams in competitions organised by the within [[Limerick GAA|Limerick County Board]] and has won several county titles in both [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]]. The club grounds are located on the [[R509 road (Ireland)|Childers Road]]. The club was relegated to intermediate status in both football and hurling following the 2010 championships. Clauaghaun returned to the [[Limerick Senior Football Championship]] after winning the 2020 [[Limerick Intermediate Football Championship]].

==Name==
The Irish name 'Clochán' is said to mean 'the place of the stepping stones', which referred to a small stream that flowed where the modern day [[N7 road (Ireland)|Dublin Road]] lies, at Clare Street.

==Hurling==
The club won its first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] in 1914, and went on the claim the title again in 1915, 1916, 1918 and 1926. In all Claughaun have won the SHC on ten occasions, the most recent title coming in 1986. 
They also won the IHC Final against South Liberties GAA in 2006.{{fact|date=July 2024}}

===Honours===

* '''[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]]''' (10): 1914, 1915, 1916, 1918, 1926, 1957, 1958, 1968, 1971, 1986
* '''Limerick Minor Hurling Championship''' (8): 1946, 1956, 1961, 1962, 1978, 1981, 1986, 1991
* '''Limerick Under-21 Hurling Championship''' (3):  1981, 1984, 1987
* '''[[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship]]''' (1): 2006
* '''[[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship]]''' (4): 1904, 1912, 1918, 1929{{fact|date=July 2024}}

===Notable players===
*[[Eamonn Cregan]], Limerick senior hurler, won the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] with the county in [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1973]], after a commanding performance at centre half-back. 
*Michael Cregan trained the 1973 Limerick team, whose panel also included Claughaun's Andy Dunworth and Mick Graham, the latter of whom missed much of the victorious campaign through injury. 
*Mickey Cross, of Claughaun, won [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Senior Hurling titles]] in 1934 and 1936 with Limerick. 
*Danny Fitzgerald won [[National Hurling League]] winner's medals in 1984 and 1985 with Limerick
*[[Mike Galligan]] won [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] medals in 1994 and 1996.
*Gus Ryan captained his county to the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]] in 1987<ref name=SM>Sean Murphy. 'The Boys of Claughaun' (2002){{isbn missing}}</ref>

==Gaelic football==
Claughaun won the [[Limerick Senior Football Championship]] for the first time in 1955, and followed up with another 13 SFC title wins over the following four decades, the last in 1996.<ref name=SM />

===Honours===
* '''[[Limerick Senior Football Championship]]''' (14): 1955, 1959, 1967, 1969, 1970, 1971, 1982, 1984, 1986, 1988, 1989, 1993, 1995, 1996<ref>{{cite web|url = https://hoganstand.com/Limerick/ClubTitles | website = hoganstand.com | title = Limerick - Club Titles | accessdate = 30 July 2024 }}</ref>

* '''Limerick Under-21 Football Championship''' (2): 1980, 1982
* '''[[Limerick Intermediate Football Championship]]''' (1): 2020<ref>{{cite web|url = https://sportinglimerick.com/intermediate-football-championship-game-of-2020-claughaun-v-gerald-griffins-final/ | website = sportinglimerick.com | title = Intermediate Football Championship Game of 2020 – Claughaun v Gerald Griffins – Final | date = 30 December 2020 | accessdate = 30 July 2024 }}</ref>

'''Ballybrown GAA''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club in [[Clarina, County Limerick|Clarina]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club is affiliated to the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick County Board]] and fields teams in [[hurling]], [[Gaelic football]] and [[camogie]].

==History==

Located in the village of [[Clarina, County Limerick|Clarina]], about 5 miles west of [[Limerick]], Ballybrown GAA Club was founded in 1890.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ballybrowngaa.com/|title=Welcome|publisher=Ballybrown GAA website|date=|access-date=6 October 2019|first=|last=}}</ref> The club spent the majority of its early existence operating in the lower grades. Ballybrown had its first notable success when, in 1913, the club won the [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship|Limerick JHC]] title. A second title was won over half a century later in 1967, while the Limerick JAFC title was won in 1981.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/81828-2/|title=Ballybrown|publisher=Limerick GAA website|date=|access-date=24 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

Ballybrown won the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] title for the first time in its history in September 1989, after a 4–10 to 2–09 win over [[Doon GAA|Doon]] in the [[1989 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/1638193/gerdie-mcgrath-they-re-the-best-doon-players-we-ve-had.html|title=Gerdie McGrath: 'They're the best Doon players we have had'|publisher=Limerick Live|date=25 October 2024|access-date=25 October 2024}}</ref> The [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] title was later claimed, before Ballybrown were beaten by [[Ballyhale Shamrocks GAA|Ballyhale Shamrocks]] by 1–16 to 0–16 in the [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|1990 All-Ireland Club SHC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=6 October 2019|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/watch-30th-anniversary-of-ballybrown-v-ballyhale-all-ireland-club-hurling-final-8092135|title=WATCH: 30th anniversary of Ballybrown v Ballyhale All-Ireland club hurling final|publisher=Limerick Live|date=17 March 2020|access-date=24 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Ballybrown won a second Limerick SHC title in 1991.

The 21st century saw Ballybrown return to the senior ranks after winning the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] title in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/limerick-ihc-final-ballybrown-v-dromin-athlacca-preview-8566203|title=Limerick IHC Final - Ballybrown v Dromin-Athlacca preview|publisher=Limerick Live|date=19 October 2012|access-date=24 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> The club later had a number of underage successes, including a three-in-a-row of Limerick Premier MHC titles between 2019 and 2021, as well as a Limerick Premier U21HC title in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/ballybrown-gaa-club-are-reaping-what-they-sowed|title=Ballybrown GAA club are reaping what they sowed |publisher=GAA website|date=18 September 2025|access-date=24 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Ballybrown beat [[Tommy Larkin's GAA|Tommy Larkin's]] by 0–14 to 1–06 to win the [[All-Ireland Junior B Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland JBHC]] title in March 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41806412.html|title=Ballybrown keep Limerick run going as they down Tommy Larkins for Junior B glory|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=8 March 2026|access-date=30 March 2026|first=Tom|last=Clancy}}</ref>

'''Croom GAA''' club is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club located in [[Croom, County Limerick|Croom]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club was founded in 1884 and fields teams in both [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]].

==Location==
The club is situated in the parish of Croom in central County Limerick in the south division on the banks of the [[River Maigue|Maigue]]. Bordering clubs include [[Granagh-Ballingarry GAA|Granagh/Ballingarry]], Croagh/Kilfinny, [[Adare GAA|Adare]], [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]], [[Crecora/Manister GAA|Crecora/Manister]] and Banogue. The club is roughly 20 km south of [[Limerick City]].

==History==
The club was founded in 1884 as Croom Abú's and is one of the oldest clubs in the county.{{fact|date=July 2024}} Croom became a force in hurling within the county, winning twenty-three West Senior Hurling titles from 1907 to 1943. During that period, they also won [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|County Senior Hurling Championships]] in 1908, 1919, 1924, 1929, 1940 and 1941 along with a Junior Hurling title in 1922 and a minor in 1936. At this time they built up a rivalry with [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] with whom they contested a number of county finals. Croom had a number of All-Ireland winners with Limerick in the early part of the 20th century, including Paddy Buskin in 1897, Mick Feely, Jack O'Shea and Ter Mangan in 1913, [[Garrett Howard]], Mick Mullane and Tom Mangan, Howard, Jim Roche and Jack O'Connell in 1934, Howard and Roche in 1936 and Peter Cregan and Roche in 1940.{{fact|date=July 2024}}

In 1950, the club could only field a junior hurling team and they were moved to the south division in 1956. They then won the County Junior Hurling Championship in 1965. Croom first fielded a junior football team in 1954 winning the County Championship in 1967. At this stage, football was becoming the dominant sport in the club. They went on to win seven South Senior Football titles winning County titles in 1976 and 1983 beating [[Oola GAA|Oola]] and St. Kieran's along with several underage titles. [[Donal Murray (hurler)|Donal Murray]] was a member of the Limerick Senior Hurling team that lost the All-Ireland final to Galway in 1980. A South Senior Hurling Crown was won in 1982 but this marked the start of a barren period for the club.{{fact|date=July 2024}}

By the mid-1990s there had been a revival in both codes at underage level.{{fact|date=July 2024}} The now junior hurlers won the County title in 1996 and won the Intermediate title two years later. Croom won back-to-back Minor County titles in 1996/97 and won a County Under-21 title in 2001 and had several players on the All-Ireland Under-21 winning teams of 2000-02. The footballers won a County Minor title in 1998 and followed it up by winning the County Under-21 titles in 1999 and 2000, along with a County junior championship in 1999. There was also three Croom footballers on the Limerick team that won their first ever [[Munster Under-21 Football Championship]] in 2000. In this period, however, Croom did not win intermediate football or senior hurling titles, losing an Intermediate Championship final in 2000 to Gerald Griffin's and a County Senior Hurling final in 2007 when they were beaten by [[Adare GAA|Adare]].{{fact|date=July 2024}}

Four Croom players, [[Stephen Lucey]], [[Peter Lawlor (hurler)|Peter Lawlor]], [[Mark O'Riordan]] and [[Hugh Flavin]], were part of the Limerick Senior Hurling team that lost the 2007 All-Ireland final. In the late 2000s-early 2010s, the club's underage teams mainly fielded 13-a-side and 11 a-side teams, often amalgamating with neighbouring parishes to field a 15-a-side team.{{fact|date=July 2024}} The hurlers lost their senior status in 2013, losing a relegation play-off to rivals [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and were regraded to play at premier intermediate level for 2014. The footballers were also relegated in 2013, after being beaten by old rivals Gerald Griffin's in the relegation playoff.{{fact|date=July 2024}}

The club is located in the parish of Fedamore which is 15km south of [[Limerick City]]. ==History==
The club was founded in 1884 making it one of the oldest GAA clubs in the county. The club won the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] in 1912 beating Ballingarry and in 1927 beating Young Ireland's. Several East Senior Championships were also won in the early 20th century.{{fact|date=May 2021}} Liam Clifford, a member of the club, was elected ninth president of the GAA, serving from 1926-1928. [[Paddy Clohessy]] won All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships in 1934, 1936 and 1940 while his brother Dave joined him in 1934 and 1936. The club had to wait until 1976 for their next significant achievement when they won the County Intermediate Hurling Championship with a win over [[Glenroe GAA|Glenroe]].{{fact|date=July 2024}} Soon after their minors amalgamated with South Liberties and reached the county final

The club did win the County Under-16 11-a-side championship in 2010 but declining numbers meant that they are amalgamated with [[Crecora/Manister GAA|Crecora/Manister]] from under-13 to minor (Kilpeacon) and with [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]] at under-21 level (St. Kevin's). Kilpeacon won the County Minor B Football Championship in 2013. Fedamore's junior B footballers won the County Junior B Football League also in 2013 but were beaten narrowly in the Championship final by Feenagh/Kilmeedy. In 2015 Fedamore won the Junior B football county championship (first adult county title in 39 years) beating rivals Crecora in the final.{{fact|date=May 2021}}

==Grounds==
The club's field was previously located in Fanningstown, 2km from the village.{{fact|date=July 2024}} However, a site was bought at Boolavoord just outside the village on the [[Croom]] road. The facilities include a full sized pitch, clubhouse and car park.{{fact|date=July 2024}}

'''Crecora/Manister''' (Irish: ''Craobh Chumhra/Mainistir'') is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club located in the parishes of [[Crecora]] and Manister in [[County Limerick]]. The club, in its current form, was founded in 1968.<ref name="clubWebsiteHistory">{{cite web|url = http://crecoramanistergaa.com/wp/4-2/club-history/ | website = crecoramanistergaa.com | title = Craobh Chumhra Mainister CLG - Club History | accessdate = 28 June 2026 }}</ref> The club fields teams in [[hurling]] from underage up to Junior A, and in [[Gaelic football]] from underage to Intermediate.

==Location==
The club is situated in the half parish of Crecora and in the parish of Manister in central County Limerick. The parishes are situated roughly 15 km south of [[Limerick City]] and are near the larger villages of [[Patrickswell]], [[Croom]] . Neighbouring clubs include Mungret St. Paul's, [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]], [[Croom GAA|Croom]], Banogue, Camogue Rovers, Fedamore and [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]].

==History==
A club was founded in the Crecora area in 1885.<ref name="clubWebsiteHistory"/> This competed in a number of tournaments at that time.{{fact|date=June 2026}} In one tournament in Ballyneety, Crecora lost to [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]] in the final.{{fact|date=June 2026}} There was also a recorded match against Liberties in Ballysheedy in 1895.{{fact|date=June 2026}} Manister also had its own club during the latter years of the 19th century. The two clubs went in and out of existence over the first half of the 20th century, and merged with other neighbouring clubs. For example, the Crecora club amalgamated with Mungret for a period, and the Manister club joined with Banogue.<ref name="clubWebsiteHistory"/>

The modern club was established in 1968 and teams initially competed at junior level.<ref name="clubWebsiteHistory"/> While the club did not initially have an underage section,<ref name="clubWebsiteHistory"/> the club started to win underage and minor titles during the late 1990s and early 2000s, including several division two titles at under-14, under-16 and minor grades.

Crecora/Manister won the County Junior B Hurling Championship in 2001 with a win over Ballybricken in the final. They reached the semi-finals of the County Junior A Hurling Championship in 2007, but thus far haven't challenged for promotion to intermediate level. In 2020 the clubs football team won their first ever Junior A County final defeating Monagea by a scoreline of 1-11 to 0-11, sealing promotion to intermediate level for the first time in the clubs history. Due to the small population of the parishes the club amalgamates with neighbouring clubs such as [[South Liberties GAA]] with some success.

==Grounds==
Until the 1980s, the club rented out various fields around the parishes from local farmers for training and matches.<ref name="clubWebsiteHistory"/> In 1988, it located a site about half a kilometre from Crecora village in the townland of Skehanagh in Manister parish.{{fact|date=June 2026}} It was blessed and officially opened in 1991 and contained a full sized pitch along with a smaller sized training pitch.{{fact|date=June 2026}} Dressing rooms were constructed between 1997 and 1998, and nets and lights were added in 2003.<ref name="clubWebsiteFacilities">{{cite web|url = http://crecoramanistergaa.com/wp/4-2/301-2/ | website = crecoramanistergaa.com | title= Craobh Chumhra Mainister CLG - Facilities | accessdate = 28 June 2026 }}</ref> A gym was opened in 2026.<ref name="clubWebsiteFacilities"/>

'''Bruff GAA''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club in [[Bruff]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club is affiliated to the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick County Board]] and fields teams in both [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]].

==History==

Located in the village of [[Bruff]], about 15 miles from [[Limerick]], Bruff GAA Club was founded in 1887. The club spent a century without any notable successes at adult level. In spite of this, Bruff appeared in [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#List of finals|Limerick SHC finals]] in the early 1920s, however, they were beaten by [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]] in 1922 and [[Newcastle West GAA|Newcastle West]] in 1925. Bruff won the Limerick MHC title for the first time in 1941.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2026/06/24/three-all-ireland-minor-wins-for-limerick/|title=Three All-Ireland Minor wins for Limerick|date=24 June 2026|publisher=Limerick Post|access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref>

A second Limerick MHC title in 1983 and a first Limerick MFC title in 1984 paved the way for future successes at adult level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-shc-final-preview-recalling-ballybrown-and-patrickswell-in-1983-8414428|title=Limerick SHC final preview – recalling Ballybrown and Patrickswell in 1983|date=20 October 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/granagh-ballingarry-gaa-club-notes-34/|title=Granagh/Ballingarry GAA club notes|date=|publisher=Limerick GAA website|access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref> Bruff celebrated its centenary by winning the Limerick JAFC title in 1987. This was followed by a [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] title in 1989 and a return to the top flight.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oldchristiansgaa.com/club-history.html|title=Club History 1955 - 2024|date=|publisher=Old Christians GAA website|access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref> Bruff had one of its most successful seasons ever when, in 2008, the club claimed a treble of Limerick Premier U21FC, Limerick JAFC and Limerick IHC honours.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/reeling-in-the-years-limerick-gaas-2008/|title=Reeling in the Years: Limerick GAA’s 2008|date=17 June 2020|publisher=Sporting Limerick|access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref> Bruff were later beaten by [[Skellig Rangers GAA|Skellig Rangers]] in the [[2008–09 All-Ireland Junior Club Football Championship#Munster final|2008 Munster Club JFC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20080157.html|title=Mallow serves up finals to savour|date=16 December 2008|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref>

Bruff once again returned to the senior ranks of Limerick hurling when they beat [[Croom GAA|Croom]] by 2–14 to 0–16 to win the [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick PIHC]] title in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/bruff-lead-the-way-on-our-premier-ihc-team-of-the-year-8537111|title=Bruff lead the way on our Premier IHC team of the year|date=31 October 2014|publisher=Limerick Live|access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref> Bruff won the [[Munster Junior B Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club JBHC]] title in 2022, following a win over [[Thurles Sarsfields GAA|Thurles Sarsfields]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/brilliant-bruff-defeat-thurles-sarsfields-to-claim-munster-junior-b-championship-title/|title=Brilliant Bruff defeat Thurles Sarsfields to claim Munster Junior B Championship title|date=28 January 2023|publisher=Sporting Limerick|access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Commercials GAA''' was a Limerick [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club which folded around 1990.

==History==

Commercials were founded in 1884 by shop assistants working in the city. Many of its members came from [[County Limerick]] and surrounding counties. In the late 19th century, many shopworkers would have come from [[smallholding|smallholder]] families as shop work was one of the few occupations open to rural Catholics with some education who had no land to inherit. Shopworkers were very active in nationalist and cultural organisations like the IRB, the Gaelic League and the GAA.{{fact|date=December 2021}}

Commercials were a dominant football team in Limerick during the early days of the GAA, and won 16 county senior championships between 1887 and 1927.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Club Titles - Limerick |url=https://hoganstand.com/Limerick/ClubTitles |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=HoganStand GAA Football and Hurling}}</ref> They won the first football All Ireland in 1887 defeating Young Irelands of Dundalk.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Keaveney |first=Mal |date=2023-06-09 |title=Limerick All-Ireland medal sells at auction |url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2023/06/09/limerick-all-ireland-medal-sells-at-auction/ |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=Limerick Post |language=en-GB}}</ref> 
The Limerick Commercials team in the 1887 All-Ireland football final (played on a field known as the "Big Bank" in Clonskeagh C. Dublin on 29 April 1888)<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Doyle |first=Siobhán |date=2023-07-27 |title=The story of the first All-Ireland football medals |url=https://www.rte.ie/brainstorm/2023/0727/1396741-first-all-ireland-football-final-1887-commercials-limerick-medals/ |journal=RTE |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-07-24 |title=Final Fling Peil 2026 |url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/final-fling-peil-2026 |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=www.gaa.ie |language=en}}</ref> was: Denis Corbett (goalkeeper and captain), Timothy Fitzgibbon, William Gunning, Richard Breen, John Hyland, Thomas McNamara, William J Spain (winner of an All-Ireland hurling medal with Dublin in 1889), Patrick J Corbett, Michael Slattery, Jeremiah R Kennedy, Michael Casey, James Mulqueen, Malachi O'Brien, Patrick Kelly, Timothy Kennedy, Philip Keating, William Cleary, Robert Normoyle, Patrick S Reeves, Thomas Keating, Thomas McMahon. Others to play for the team in previous rounds were Ned Nicholas, Edward Casey, Richard O'Brien, James Purcell, Thomas McLoughlin and Thomas Lynch.<ref name=":1" /> After trailing by 0-3 to 0-1 to the Dundalk team at half-time, they came back to win by 1-4 to 0-3.<ref name=":2" />

Commercials added a second All Ireland title in 1896 defeating another Young Irelands from Dublin. They won a number of City Division junior football titles during the 1950s and appeared in a final for the last time in 1961.{{fact|date=December 2021}} Young Irelands and Commercials joined in the 1950s as sister clubs with Young Irelands running the hurling and Commercials the football but with no field of their own and a hit and miss underage structure, they struggled to survive until they finally folded up around 1990.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Connaughton |first=Gary |date=2025-08-27 |title=11 Of The Most Successful GAA Clubs That No Longer Exist |url=https://www.balls.ie/gaa/10-most-successful-gaa-clubs-no-longer-exist-638783 |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=Balls.ie |language=en}}</ref>

'''Dromin/Athlacca''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club located in [[Athlacca]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club fields teams in both [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]].

==History==

Hurling in the locality dates back to 1887 when a Dromin team fielded a team in one of the first tournaments organised under [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]] rules.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://drominathlacca.wordpress.com/sporting-history/|title=Sporting History|publisher=Dromin/Athlacca website|date=|access-date=13 October 2021|first=|last=}}</ref> The club has enjoyed multiple county championship successes in the 21st century, having claimed four [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|County Intermediate Championship]] titles.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/89818/Dromin-Athlacca-crowned-Limerick-IHC-winners.html|title=Dromin-Athlacca crowned Limerick IHC winners|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=15 October 2013|access-date=29 September 2021|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/344571/dromin-athlacca-win-limerick-ihc-against-13-man-croom.html|title=Dromin-Athlacca win Limerick IHC against 13 man Croom|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=27 October 2018|access-date=29 September 2021|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

==Honours==

*[[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship]]: [[2023 Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|2023]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41257921.html|title=Last gasp Breen the hero as Dromin Athlacca seal Limerick Premier Intermediate title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=28 October 2023|access-date=28 October 2023|first=Tom|last=Clancy}}</ref>, [[2026 Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|2026]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-25 |title=Dromin-Athlacca withstand late Bruff rally to secure Premier IHC title |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/dromin-athlacca-withstand-late-bruff-rally-to-secure-premier-ihc-title-9308359 |access-date=2026-10-26 |website=Limerick Live |language=en}}</ref>
*[[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship]]: 1977, 2004, 2007, 2013, 2018
*[[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship]]: 1995

'''Commercials Hurling & Camogie Club''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club located in [[Rathcoole, County Dublin|Rathcoole]], [[County Dublin]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club is concerned with the games of [[hurling]] and [[camogie]].

==History==

Commercials Hurling Club was established in 1886. The club was home to the many bar and shop workers who had moved from to Dublin from rural Ireland seeking employment. The club first played their matches in Dublin city centre and, like a lot of clubs at the time, they trained in the [[Phoenix Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://commercialshurlingclub.com/content_page/10025424/|title=About us - history|date=|work=Commercials GAA website|accessdate=12 November 2022}}</ref>

The club was less than a decade in existence when Commercials claimed its first [[Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|Dublin SHC]] in 1895. It was the first of a record five successive titles. In all, Commercials won nine titles in the first 30 years of their existence.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/dublin/ClubTitles|title=Club titles - Dublin|date=|work=Hogan Stand|accessdate=12 November 2022}}</ref> Successes in the lower grades was also achieved, with [[Dublin Intermediate Hurling Championship|Dublin IHC]] and [[Dublin Junior Hurling Championship|Dublin JHC]] titles being secured on a number of occasions.

==Honours==

*'''[[Dublin Senior Hurling Championship]]''' (9): 1895, 1896, 1897, 1898, 1899, [[1905 Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|1905]], [[1907 Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|1907]], [[1909 Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|1909]], [[1916 Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|1916]]
*'''[[Dublin Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship]]''' (1): 2025
*'''[[Dublin Intermediate Hurling Championship]]''' (6): 1928, 1932, 1964, 1977, 1991, 2024
*'''[[Dublin Junior Hurling Championship]]''' (3): 1899, 1925, 1940, 2022<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/dublin-gaa/commercials-take-jhc-a-honours-with-impressive-16-point-success-against-lucan-sarsfields-42091058.html|title=Commercials take JHC ‘A’ honours with impressive 16-point success against Lucan Sarsfields|date=24 October 2022|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=12 November 2022}}</ref>

'''Feenagh–Kilmeedy GAA''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club located in the village of [[Feenagh, County Limerick|Feenagh]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club fields teams in both [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]].

==History==

Located in the village of [[Feenagh, County Limerick|Feenagh]], on the [[County Cork|Cork]]-[[County Limerick|Limerick]] border, Feenagh–Kilmeedy GAA Club was founded in 1955, however, [[Gaelic games]] had been played in the area since the foundation of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. The club has spent most of its existence operating in the junior grade, winning its first [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship|Limerick JHC]] title in 1962. Promoted to the senior ranks the following year, Feenagh-Kilmeedy won the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] title at the first attempt, beating divisional side [[Emmets GAA|Emmets]] in the [[1963 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|final]] by 3-06 to 3-01.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20102440.html|title=Coach Carroll’s Emmetts bid to restore bruised Limerick pride|accessdate=3 October 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=30 October 2023|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://hoganstand.com/Limerick/ClubTitles|title=Club Titles - Limerick|accessdate=|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=30 October 2023|first=|last=}}</ref> The club regraded in 1967 and added further JHC titles in 1989, 2003 and 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2023/10/29/junior-championship-continues-to-excite/|title=Junior Championship continues to excite|accessdate=29 October 2023 |publisher=Limerick Post|date=30 October 2023|first=Mal|last=Keaveney}}</ref> Feenagh–Kilmeedy's junior football team won Limerick JBFC titles in 2003 and 2013, before claiming the JAFC title in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2021/11/01/fr-caseys-and-feenagh-kilmeedy-capture-junior-football-championship-titles/|title=Fr Caseys and Feenagh Kilmeedy capture Junior Football Championship titles|accessdate=2 November 2021 |publisher=Limerick Post|date=30 October 2023|first=Jack|last=Neville}}</ref> The club became the inaugural winners of the new [[Limerick Premier Junior A Hurling Championship|Limerick PJAHC]] title after beating [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St Patrick's]] in 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/1640461/feenagh-kilmeedy-edge-past-st-patrick-s-in-thrilling-limerick-premier-junior-hurling-final.html|title=Feenagh-Kilmeedy edge past St Patrick's in thrilling Limerick premier junior 'A' hurling final|publisher=Limerick Live|date=26 October 2024|access-date=27 October 2024|first=|last=}}</ref>

*'''[[Limerick Premier Junior A Hurling Championship]]''' (1): [[2024 Limerick Premier Junior A Hurling Championship|2024]]

'''Emmets GAA''' was a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] division located in south [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The division was primarily concerned with the game of [[hurling]].

==History==

Divisional Boards in Limerick were created at the start of the 20th century, with the South Board being formed in 1924. The notion of divisional teams taking part in the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|SHC]] and [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|SFC]] is believed to have first been suggested in the late 1940s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vsopublicationsltd.ie/down-memory-lane-four-county-titles-for-western-gaels-in-a-glorious-ten-year-spell/|title=Down Memory Lane – Four county titles for Western Gaels in a glorious ten year spell|publisher=Vale Star|date=4 June 2020|access-date=31 October 2024}}</ref> These divisional teams would be composed of players from the various juvenile and intermediate clubs within the division. The divisional system had been operated by [[Cork GAA]] in their competitions since the 1930s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41495513.html|title=Watch: Denis Ring on Cork divisional debate — 'It was never raised as a question until Imokilly started to win'|date=14 October 2024|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41577367.html|title=Reform or removal: The age old debate around divisions in Cork GAA|date=21 February 2025|publisher=Echo Live|access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref>

Emmets, as the division became known as, reached the SHC final for the first time in [[1963 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|1963]], but were beaten by 3-06 to 3-01 by [[Feenagh-Kilmeedy GAA|Feenagh-Kilmeedy]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20102440.html|title=Coach Carroll's Emmetts bid to restore bruised Limerick pride|accessdate=3 October 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=30 October 2023|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://hoganstand.com/Limerick/ClubTitles|title=Club Titles - Limerick|accessdate=|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=30 October 2023|first=|last=}}</ref> Emmets reached a second final in 2010, but lost after a 1–16 to 1–12 defeat by [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/corkman/localnotes/kilmallock-win-a-ninth-senior-hurling-title-27080277.html|title=Kilmallock win a ninth Senior hurling title|publisher=The Corkman|date=7 October 2010|access-date=15 October 2018}}</ref>

'''Galbally GAA''' is a [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] club in [[Galbally, County Limerick|Galbally]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. The club, based at Cussen Memorial Park is exclusively concerned with the game of [[Gaelic football]], but previously fielded teams in [[hurling]].

==History==

Located in the village of [[Galbally, County Limerick|Galbally]], on the [[County Limerick|Limerick]]–[[County Tipperary|Tipperary]] border, Galbally GAA Club was founded in 1905. The club has spent most of its existence operating in the junior grade, however, there have also been periods where the club lapsed for a number of reasons.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://galballygaa.wordpress.com/club-history/|title=Club history|publisher=Galbally GAA website|date=|access-date=4 December 2025}}</ref>

Galbally had its first major success when, in 1968, the club claimed the Limerick JAFC title. Further success followed in 1990, when Galbally won the [[Limerick Intermediate Football Championship|Limerick IFC]] title and secured senior status for the first time.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/Limerick/Article/Index/294422|title=Galbally club notes|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=21 January 2019|access-date=4 December 2025}}</ref> Four years later the club claimed its inaugural [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|Limerick SFC]] title, after a 3–17 to 1–13 win over [[Father Casey's GAA|Fr Casey's]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/229404|title=Galbally club notes|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=22 December 2014|access-date=4 December 2025}}</ref> A second Limerick SFC followed three years later, when Galbally were awarded the title following an objection after [[University of Limerick]] won the title on the field of play.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.southernstar.ie/sport/the-inside-track-good-times-when-we-put-ul-footballers-on-the-limerick-gaa-map-4226390|title=THE INSIDE TRACK: Good times when we put UL footballers on the Limerick GAA map|publisher=The Southern Star|date=10 July 2021|access-date=4 December 2025}}</ref>

The club fielded a hurling team between 1982 and 2000, and won the Limerick JBHC title in 1995. Further Limerick IFC titles were won in 2010 and 2018.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.live95fm.ie/news/sport/galbally-return-to-senior-football-ranks/|title=Galbally return to Senior Football ranks|publisher=Live 95fm|date=24 October 2018|access-date=4 December 2025}}</ref>

* '''[[Limerick Intermediate Football Championship]]''' (3): 1990, 2010, 2018

* '''Limerick Junior B Hurling Championship''' (1): 1995
